title: Drop empty entries: a new list with filter, in place with removeIf

blocks.text: There are two ways to drop unwanted elements. `stream().filter(predicate)` builds a **new** list and leaves the source alone. `collection.removeIf(predicate)` changes the collection **in place**, with no iterator and no `ConcurrentModificationException`. `Predicate.not(String::isBlank)` reads well in a filter.
Write two methods in `Cleaner`. An entry is empty when it is `null` or has no visible text.

items: `meaningful(List<String> items)` returns a new list of the non-empty entries, in order.
`prune(List<String> names)` removes the empty entries from `names` itself and returns how many it removed.

blocks.text: The page's own example list is `["Alice", "", "Bob", null, "  ", "Charlie"]`.

cases.says: Entries with text survive, in order; empty strings are dropped, and prune reports how many it removed.
A null entry is dropped without a NullPointerException.
An entry of only spaces or tabs has no text and is dropped.
meaningful builds a new list; the caller's list keeps every entry.

concepts: Predicate.not negates a method reference such as String::isBlank directly.
removeIf deletes matching elements in place, while filter builds a new collection and leaves the source alone.
